cefrAlignment: Fits the B2 phonological control descriptors ('can generally use appropriate intonation, place stress correctly and articulate individual sounds clearly'); the focus on focus-word shift, fall-rise and connected speech (linking, weak forms, elision, assimilation) matches B2 learners, and the features are explained accurately.
examFidelity: TOEIC Read a text aloud uses the correct 45 s prep / 45 s reading (68-word text fits easily); TOEFL Listen and Repeat and IELTS Part 1 advice matches exams.ts; the IELTS pronunciation tip now paraphrases the public descriptors instead of misquoting them.
fixes: IELTS tip corrected: it attributed 'a wide range of pronunciation features' to band 7; the public descriptors use 'wide range of phonological features' at band 8 (band 7 = some band-8 features), so it now refers to the higher bands and the descriptor's own wording
Made list intonation consistent: the TOEIC tip said 'rise, rise, fall' while the table and checklist taught fall-rise; now 'a rise or fall-rise on each item, a fall on the last'
Walkthrough focus words corrected: it put the list fall-rise and fall on 'walk' and 'friends', contradicting the lesson's own 'last content word' rule; now 'hills' and 'park'

TOEIC read-aloud instructions no longer tell learners to 'mark' the text (a computer-delivered test has nothing to mark); they now say to read silently and decide where focus words, pauses and lists are
Softened the unsupported key point 'Shadowing is the fastest way' to 'one of the most effective ways'
openConcerns: The model answer and all six shadowing sentences are spoken by browser TTS. The walkthrough describes specific tones (two falls on 'OUTdoors, DEFinitely', fall-rise on 'hills', weak forms, elision of /t/ in 'just want'), and TTS may not produce them. A specialist should check the TTS output or replace it with a human recording (the audio section supports `src`)
The read-aloud announcement uses US forms (parking lot, dollars) in an otherwise British-spelling lesson; this is deliberate for a US store, but worth a glance
learnerOutcome: A learner can put the main stress on the focus word (and move it for contrast), choose falling, rising or fall-rise intonation, use common linking and weak forms, and read a short announcement aloud with natural chunking.
